page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Motion in a Straight Line · 2 marks

steps.label: Speed
lines: Speed is the rate at which distance is
It is a scalar and is never negative.
steps.why: Speed is built from distance, which never decreases, so speed can never be negative. The speed itself can still rise and fall during the motion.

recall.must_convey: That speed is distance divided by time and is a scalar.

steps.memory_tip: Speed comes from distance. Velocity comes from displacement.

steps.label: Velocity
lines: It is a vector, so it has direction, and it
can be negative or zero. Average velocity is
steps.why: Because velocity is built from displacement, every property of displacement carries over: direction, sign, and zero for a round trip.
common_mistakes: Saying average speed always equals the magnitude of average velocity. They are equal only when the body moves along one straight line in one direction, without reversing.

recall.must_convey: That velocity is displacement divided by time, is a vector, and is zero on average for a round trip.

steps.memory_tip: Swap distance for displacement and speed becomes velocity.
steps.margin_note: Mirror the wording of the speed line so the contrast reads.

insider_note: Pair it with the distance and displacement contrast — speed is built on one, velocity on the other.
